label: Rushmere Reading Project — outcomes nested two levels deep
covers: The OUTCOMES column carries TWO levels of in-column heading above its items: a section ('For young people') and a sub-section under it ('While they are with us'), then the bullets. The regression set records this shape as the one that churns — the README traces a document moving 111 to 115 items under an UNCHANGED prompt to nesting four levels deep in its outcome columns, and names it as the model re-rolling an underdetermined choice about how to flatten 3-4 source levels into this schema's two (Group.name -> items[]), which nothing in the prompt specifies. Both heading levels are declared as labels, so a run that folds them either way still scores 100% on items in columns; what this document makes visible is whether the ITEMS survive the flattening, which is the launch gate's question and the one no synthetic document in the set previously asked.

columns.heading: INPUTS
items: Staffing
A part-time reading coordinator based at the library
Six trained volunteer reading partners
Materials
A rotating collection of four hundred levelled readers
Printed reading records for every child enrolled

columns.heading: ACTIVITIES
items: Weekly one-to-one reading sessions of thirty minutes
A half-term family reading morning at the library
Termly training refreshers for the volunteer partners

columns.heading: OUTPUTS
items: Around six hundred reading sessions delivered each year
Three family reading mornings held across the year

columns.heading: OUTCOMES
items: For young people
While they are with us
Children choose a book without being prompted
Children read aloud to an adult without visible anxiety
After they leave us
Children keep a library membership of their own
Children move up a reading band by the end of the year
For families
While they are with us
Parents and carers hear their child read at home each week
After they leave us
Families visit the library together outside session times
